title: Joshua 15
paragraphs: ¹ The allotment for the tribe of Judah by its clans extended down to the territory of Edom, to the wilderness of Zin in the far south. ² Their southern boundary started from the southern tip of the Dead Sea, ³ ran south of the Scorpion Pass, continued to Zin, went up south of Kadesh Barnea, past Hezron, up to Addar and curved around to Karka. ⁴ From there it passed along to Azmon and went out to the Wadi of Egypt, ending at the sea. That is your southern boundary. ⁵ The eastern boundary was the Dead Sea as far as the mouth of the Jordan. The northern boundary began at the bay at the mouth of the Jordan,

⁶ went up to Beth Hoglah and continued north of Beth Arabah; then it went up to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben. ⁷ From the Valley of Achor the boundary went up toward Debir, then turned north toward Gilgal, which faces the Pass of Adummim south of the ravine, continued to the waters of En Shemesh, and ended at En Rogel. ⁸ Then the boundary went up through the Valley of Ben Hinnom to the southern slope of the Jebusite ridge — that is, Jerusalem. From there it climbed to the top of the hill on the western edge of the Hinnom Valley, at the northern end of the Valley of Rephaim. ⁹ From there the boundary curved from the hilltop to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah, came out near the towns of Mount Ephron, and then curved to Baalah, which is Kiriath Jearim. ¹⁰ From Baalah the boundary turned westward to Mount Seir, continued along the northern slope of Mount Jearim — that is, Kesalon — went down to Beth Shemesh, and passed along to Timnah.

¹¹ The boundary continued to the northern slope of Ekron, curved to Shikkeron, passed along to Mount Baalah, and went out to Jabneel, ending at the sea. ¹² The western boundary was the coastline of the Mediterranean Sea. These are the boundaries on all sides for the clans of Judah. ¹³ In keeping with the LORD's command to Joshua, Caleb son of Jephunneh was given a portion among the people of Judah — Kiriath Arba, that is, Hebron. (Arba was the father of Anak.) ¹⁴ From there Caleb drove out the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai. ¹⁵ From there he marched against the people living in Debir, which was formerly called Kiriath Sepher.

¹⁶ Caleb said, I will give my daughter Achsah in marriage to the man who attacks and captures Kiriath Sepher. ¹⁷ Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's brother, took it, and Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah in marriage. ¹⁸ One day when she came to Othniel, she urged him to ask her father for a field. She got down from her donkey, and Caleb asked her, What do you want? ¹⁹ She answered, Give me a blessing — you've given me land in the Negev; give me springs of water too. So he gave her the upper springs and the lower springs. ²⁰ This is the inheritance of the tribe of Judah by its clans.

²¹ The cities farthest south belonging to the tribe of Judah toward the border of Edom were Kabzeel, Eder, Jagur, ²² Kinah, Dimonah, Adadah, ²³ Kedesh, Hazor, Ithnan, ²⁴ Ziph, Telem, Bealoth, ²⁵ Hazor Hadattah, Kerioth Hezron (that is, Hazor),
²⁶ Amam, Shema, Moladah, ²⁷ Hazar Gaddah, Heshmon, Beth Pelet, ²⁸ Hazar Shual, Beersheba, Biziothiah, ²⁹ Baalah, Iim, Ezem, ³⁰ Eltolad, Kesil, Hormah,

³¹ Ziklag, Madmannah, Sansannah, ³² Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain, and Rimmon — twenty-nine towns in all, with their surrounding villages. ³³ In the western foothills: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah, ³⁴ Zanoah, En Gannim, Tappuah, Enam, ³⁵ Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah,

³⁶ Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah, and Gederothaim — fourteen towns with their villages. ³⁷ Zenan, Hadashah, Migdal Gad, ³⁸ Dilean, Mizpeh, Joktheel, ³⁹ Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon, ⁴⁰ Cabbon, Lahmam, Kitlish,

⁴¹ Gederoth, Beth Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah — sixteen towns with their villages. ⁴² Libnah, Ether, Ashan, ⁴³ Iphtah, Ashnah, Nezib, ⁴⁴ Keilah, Achzib, and Mareshah — nine towns with their villages. ⁴⁵ Ekron, with its surrounding settlements and villages.

⁴⁶ West of Ekron, all the towns near Ashdod with their villages; ⁴⁷ Ashdod with its towns and villages; Gaza with its towns and villages as far as the Wadi of Egypt, and the coastline of the Mediterranean Sea. ⁴⁸ In the hill country: Shamir, Jattir, Socoh, ⁴⁹ Dannah, Kiriath Sannah (that is, Debir), ⁵⁰ Anab, Eshtemoh, Anim,

⁵¹ Goshen, Holon, and Giloh — eleven towns with their villages. ⁵² Arab, Dumah, Eshan, ⁵³ Janim, Beth Tappuah, Aphekah, ⁵⁴ Humtah, Kiriath Arba (that is, Hebron), and Zior — nine towns with their villages. ⁵⁵ Maon, Carmel, Ziph, Juttah,

⁵⁶ Jezreel, Jokdeam, Zanoah, ⁵⁷ Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah — ten towns with their villages. ⁵⁸ Halhul, Beth Zur, Gedor, ⁵⁹ Maarath, Beth Anoth, and Eltekon — six towns with their villages. ⁶⁰ Kiriath Baal (that is, Kiriath Jearim) and Rabbah — two towns with their villages.

⁶¹ In the wilderness: Beth Arabah, Middin, Secacah, ⁶² Nibshan, the City of Salt, and En Gedi — six towns with their villages. ⁶³ As for the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the people of Judah could not drive them out, and the Jebusites live alongside the people of Judah in Jerusalem to this day.
